name: Numeric Truncation Error
principle: A value is cast or assigned from a wider primitive numeric type to a narrower primitive type, losing high-order bits. The truncated value can corrupt state or become an unsafe size, index, or loop bound.
detection_signals: explicit cast from long/long long/size_t/uint64_t to int/short/char
implicit assignment from wider integer type to narrower integer variable
Java cast syntax (short) intVar, (byte) intVar, or (int) longVar
truncated variable later used in malloc/calloc/realloc/new array size
truncated variable later used as array index, pointer offset, or loop bound
negative_signals: pre-cast check value >= TARGET_MIN && value <= TARGET_MAX
Java Math.toIntExact(longVal) used instead of (int) longVal
C++ gsl::narrow<T>(value) or equivalent checked narrowing used
target type is same width or wider than source type: sizeof(dst_type) >= sizeof(src_type)
truncated value is only used for intentional bit masking after an explicit mask such as value & 0xFF
false_defense_traps: Checking only value < MAX without checking value >= MIN for signed target types
Relying on explicit casts to make narrowing safe
Testing only on 32-bit builds while size_t/long becomes wider on 64-bit builds
Validating the original wide value, then using the later truncated value as the index or size
Assuming Java/C# casts throw on overflow; narrowing casts silently truncate unless checked APIs/context are used
verification_focus: Does any wider numeric value narrow to a smaller primitive type without a complete range check before the narrowed value is used?

consequence_chains.trigger: length or count is truncated before buffer allocation
consequence_chains.consequence: buffer allocated too small, then out-of-bounds write

consequence_chains.trigger: truncated value is used as an array index or pointer offset
truncated value is used as a read index or length

patch_principle: Avoid narrowing conversions from wider primitive numeric types to smaller primitive types.
If narrowing is required, check the value against the exact target type min and max before casting.
Use checked conversion APIs such as Math.toIntExact or gsl::narrow where available.
Keep sizes, indexes, and loop bounds in sufficiently wide types such as size_t.
On range failure, reject the input or throw an error instead of silently truncating.

minimal_examples.safe: int amountSold = getAmount(); if (amountSold >= Short.MIN_VALUE && amountSold <= Short.MAX_VALUE) { short sold = (short)amountSold; } else { throw new IllegalArgumentException(); }
